data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for preparing for, responding to, and reporting cybersecurity incidents.
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for preparing for, responding to, and reporting cybersecurity incidents

policy_statements.source_text: Cybersecurity incident management governs the activities for mitigating risks from such incidents before substantial harm occurs and provides timely notification to and consultation with appropriate entities.
policy_statements.target: activities for mitigating risks from such incidents

policy_statements.source_text: It is the policy of USDA to comply with Federal requirements to establish, implement, and enforce an incident management policy to continually manage risks to USDA information resources.
policy_statements.target: Federal requirements

policy_statements.source_text: This policy complies with the requirements of:
The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA);
cross_references: The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA)

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-130, Responsibilities for Protecting Federal Information Resources, Memoranda M-19-02, Fiscal Year 2018-2019 Guidance on Federal Information Security and Privacy Management Requirements, and M-17-12, Preparing for and Responding to a Breach of Personally Identifiable Information;
cross_references: The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-130, Responsibilities for Protecting Federal Information Resources
Memoranda M-19-02, Fiscal Year 2018-2019 Guidance on Federal Information Security and Privacy Management Requirements
M-17-12, Preparing for and Responding to a Breach of Personally Identifiable Information

policy_statements.source_text: The Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems; and
cross_references: The Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems

policy_statements.source_text: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53 Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations, and NIST SP 800-61 Revision 2, Computer Security Incident Handling Guide.
cross_references: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53 Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations
NIST SP 800-61 Revision 2, Computer Security Incident Handling Guide

policy_statements.source_text: This policy serves as the foundation on which USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will develop and implement their own incident management procedures that comply with Federal and Departmental requirements and align with USDA’s incident management policy.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This policy supersedes DR 3505-005, USDA Cyber Security Incident Management Policy, dated October 31, 2013, in its entirety.
cross_references: DR 3505-005, USDA Cyber Security Incident Management Policy

policy_statements.source_text: This policy is effective immediately and remains in effect until it is superseded or expires.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their incident management procedures with this policy within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: their incident management procedures
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: Terminology in this policy will be used and interpreted as follows:
The term “misuse” broadly refers to improper usage of information or information resources in violation of rules, regulations, or policies;
The terms “potential,” “suspected,” and “imminent” with respect to threats and incidents are distinct.
“Potential” refers to a currently unrealized ability and is nearly synonymous with “possible;” an example is a potential threat.

“Suspected” implies a slight indication that something might be true or there is a reasonable basis for believing so; in other words, incidents may be suspected, as opposed to being confirmed (positively identified) or actual.

“Imminent,” as explained by NIST SP 800-61 Revision 2, refers to a situation in which there is a factual basis for believing that a specific event is about to occur; attacks from a zero-day exploit of a vulnerability can be imminent;
cross_references: NIST SP 800-61 Revision 2

policy_statements.source_text: The terms “response” and “incident response” may be specific and narrow or general and broad in meaning.

The general and broad meaning encompasses multiple incident management activities, including analysis, notification, mitigation, or application of countermeasures, containment, eradication, and recovery.
The specific and narrow meaning is any one of these activities.
NIST uses the terms “incident response” and “incident handling” as synonyms; and
The term “United States Computer Emergency Readiness Team” (US-CERT) will be used as a replacement for “the Federal information security incident center” identified in FISMA.
cross_references: FISMA

policy_statements.source_text: OMB Circular A-130 requires Federal Agencies to undertake a set of actions to ensure they can react appropriately to information security incidents.
cross_references: OMB Circular A-130

policy_statements.source_text: The set includes implementing policies and procedures; establishing roles and responsibilities; maintaining incident response capabilities and mechanisms; reporting; periodic testing of the procedures; documenting lessons learned; and verifying that corrective actions are implemented.
FISMA directs Federal Agencies to develop and implement cyber incident management programs.
cross_references: FISMA

policy_statements.source_text: FISMA also imposes on Federal Agencies notification measures to be taken during major incidents and annual incident reporting requirements.
cross_references: FISMA

policy_statements.source_text: FISMA assigns responsibility to the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for developing and overseeing the implementation of binding (i.e., compulsory) operational directives to Federal Agencies to implement OMB-issued policies, principles, standards, and guidelines on information security in general.
cross_references: FISMA

policy_statements.source_text: This policy applies to:
All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA;
All Federal information, in any medium or form, generated, collected, provided, transmitted, stored, maintained, or accessed by, or on behalf of, USDA;

Information systems or services (including cloud-based services) used or operated by USDA, USDA contractors, or other organizations on behalf of, or funded by, USDA and interconnections between or among systems or services;
Cyber-based information, including electronic data, voice, and video; and
All incidents affecting personally identifiable information (PII), whether cyber-related or non-cyber related.

Nothing in this policy alters the requirements for the protection of information associated with national security systems, such as those identified in FISMA, policies, directives, instructions, and standards issued by the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), or the intelligence community.
cross_references: FISMA
policy_statements.target: requirements for the protection of information associated with national security systems

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will comply with all Federal laws and regulations, OMB policies and requirements, DHS binding operational directives, NIST standards and guidance, and Departmental directives and guidance on cybersecurity incident management.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: all Federal laws and regulations, OMB policies and requirements, DHS binding operational directives, NIST standards and guidance, and Departmental directives and guidance on cybersecurity incident management

policy_statements.source_text: Personnel with incident management responsibilities will be technically qualified and have clearances appropriate to the categorization or classification of the systems they support and the types of incident-related information they may receive.
policy_statements.target: categorization or classification of the systems they support
conditions: appropriate to the categorization or classification of the systems they support and the types of incident-related information they may receive

policy_statements.source_text: The Agriculture Security Operations Division (ASOD) Cybersecurity Incident Response Team (CSIRT) will operate as USDA’s central cybersecurity incident management group to:

Serve as the contact and coordination point with internal USDA offices, including the USDA Privacy Office, OIG, Office of Homeland Security (OHS) Personnel and Document Security Division (PDSD), and the OHS Insider Threat Program;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agriculture Security Operations Division (ASOD) Cybersecurity Incident Response Team (CSIRT)
policy_statements.target: internal USDA offices

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as USDA’s cybersecurity incident management operational liaison and point of contact with external entities such as US-CERT; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Agriculture Security Operations Division (ASOD) Cybersecurity Incident Response Team (CSIRT)
policy_statements.target: external entities such as US-CERT
policy_statements.resulting_status: USDA’s cybersecurity incident management operational liaison and point of contact

policy_statements.source_text: Act as the collection point and clearinghouse for cybersecurity incident information and have enterprise reporting responsibility related to all cybersecurity incidents, including forwarding cybersecurity incident information to US-CERT.
policy_statements.actor_name: Agriculture Security Operations Division (ASOD) Cybersecurity Incident Response Team (CSIRT)
policy_statements.target: cybersecurity incident information

policy_statements.source_text: All suspected or actual incidents will be reported to the ASOD CSIRT within 1 hour of discovery.
policy_statements.target: All suspected or actual incidents
conditions: within 1 hour of discovery

policy_statements.source_text: Examples of reportable incidents are:

Suspected or actual spillage of classified national security information (CNSI) or suspected or actual cybersecurity incidents affecting classified systems, with concurrent reporting to OHS PDSD, the Mission Area, agency, or staff office Information Security Coordinator (ISC), and Mission Area, agency, or staff office information security support staff;
Suspected or actual unauthorized release of controlled unclassified information (CUI);

Suspected or actual exposure or compromise of PII (a category of CUI) in all forms (e.g., cyber-based, verbal discussions of PII with unauthorized persons, loss of hardcopy documents that contain PII), whether the exposure is inadvertent or intentional;
Suspected or actual incidents related to criminal activity or misuse, in accordance with DR 1700-002, OIG Organization and Procedures;
cross_references: DR 1700-002, OIG Organization and Procedures

policy_statements.source_text: Suspected or actual insider threats where an insider is using or may be using his or her access to do harm, wittingly or unwittingly, to the security of the United States, including damage to the United States through espionage, terrorism, unauthorized disclosure of national security information, or the loss or degradation of Departmental resources or capabilities; and
Suspected or actual incidents of compromise to the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of USDA information, information systems, or information services.
Information regarding an incident and the investigation will be logged into the ASOD CSIRT and, if necessary, the Mission Area, agency, or staff office incident tracking mechanism.
policy_statements.target: Information regarding an incident and the investigation

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT will prioritize incidents using the management process identified in NIST SP 800-61 and in accordance with the impact classification factors and levels detailed in the DHS US-CERT Federal Incident Notification Guidelines and report to US-CERT within 1 hour:
cross_references: NIST SP 800-61
DHS US-CERT Federal Incident Notification Guidelines

policy_statements.source_text: Suspected or actual exposure or compromise of cyber-based PII;
policy_statements.target: cyber-based PII

policy_statements.source_text: Suspected or actual cyber incidents related to criminal activity or misuse; and
policy_statements.target: criminal activity or misuse

policy_statements.source_text: All actual incidents of compromise to the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of USDA information, information systems, or information services.
policy_statements.target: USDA information, information systems, or information services

policy_statements.actor_name: Senior Agency Official for CNSI/Director of OHS and the USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
policy_statements.target: any system on which CNSI is spilled

policy_statements.source_text: All suspected and actual breaches will be handled in accordance with Federal and Departmental requirements, including FISMA, OMB M-17-12, NIST SP 800-122, Guide to Protecting the Confidentiality of Personally Identifiable Information (PII), and the USDA Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Core Incident Response Group (CIRG) PII Breach Notification & Incident Response Plan (IRP), Revision 4.6.
cross_references: FISMA
OMB M-17-12
NIST SP 800-122, Guide to Protecting the Confidentiality of Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
USDA Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Core Incident Response Group (CIRG) PII Breach Notification & Incident Response Plan (IRP), Revision 4.6
policy_statements.target: All suspected and actual breaches

policy_statements.source_text: Any technology used to capture, collect, store, analyze, transmit, or access sensitive incident information, including PII, will be properly secured to preserve confidentiality and integrity.
policy_statements.target: Any technology used to capture, collect, store, analyze, transmit, or access sensitive incident information, including PII

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will:
Regularly run automated tools that are updated with current indicators of compromise (IOC) supplied by ASOD; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: automated tools that are updated with current indicators of compromise (IOC) supplied by ASOD

policy_statements.source_text: Incident management personnel will investigate all suspected and actual incidents reported by US-CERT, the ASOD CSIRT, users (whether Federal employees, contractors, or others), system, network, or database administrators, or personnel from other organizations internal or external to USDA.
policy_statements.target: all suspected and actual incidents

not later than 7 days after a major incident has been declared

policy_statements.source_text: A plan of action and milestones (POA&M) will be created for any incident and associated with either an information system or service or an information security program if:
The incident remains open (unresolved) after 30 days or if the agency or staff office anticipates that it will require more than 30 days to remediate and close;
A review determines remedial actions are or were inadequate for incident closure; or
Required information pertaining to the incident has not been submitted.

Incident management personnel will finalize the Agriculture Department (AD)-3043, ASOC Incident Report, or the AD-3038, Cyber Security Incident Report Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Incident, and submit it to close the incident with the ASOD CSIRT.
cross_references: Agriculture Department (AD)-3043, ASOC Incident Report
AD-3038, Cyber Security Incident Report Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Incident

(3) The Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems; and
(4) The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53 Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations, and NIST SP 800-61 Revision 2, Computer Security Incident Handling Guide.
d. This policy serves as the foundation on which USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will develop and implement their own incident management procedures that comply with Federal and Departmental requirements and align with USDA’s incident management policy.

Terminology in this policy will be used and interpreted as follows:
The term “misuse” broadly refers to improper usage of information or information resources in violation of rules, regulations, or policies;
The terms “potential,” “suspected,” and “imminent” with respect to threats and incidents are distinct.
“Potential” refers to a currently unrealized ability and is nearly synonymous with “possible;” an example is a potential threat.

“Suspected” implies a slight indication that something might be true or there is a reasonable basis for believing so; in other words, incidents may be suspected, as opposed to being confirmed (positively identified) or actual.

“Imminent,” as explained by NIST  SP 800-61 Revision 2,  refers to a situation in which there is a factual basis for believing that a specific event is about to occur; attacks from a zero-day exploit of a vulnerability can be imminent;
The terms “response” and “incident response” may be specific and narrow or general and broad in meaning.

The general and broad meaning encompasses multiple incident management activities, including analysis, notification, mitigation, or application of countermeasures, containment, eradication, and recovery.
The specific and narrow meaning is any one of these activities.
NIST uses the terms “incident response” and “incident handling” as synonyms; and
The term “United States Computer Emergency Readiness Team” (US-CERT) will be used as a replacement for “the Federal information security incident center” identified in FISMA.
OMB Circular A-130 requires Federal Agencies to undertake a set of actions to ensure they can react appropriately to information security incidents.

The set includes implementing policies and procedures; establishing roles and responsibilities; maintaining incident response capabilities and mechanisms; reporting; periodic testing of the procedures; documenting lessons learned; and verifying that corrective actions are implemented.
FISMA directs Federal Agencies to develop and implement cyber incident management programs.
FISMA also imposes on Federal Agencies notification measures to be taken during major incidents and annual incident reporting requirements.

FISMA assigns responsibility to the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for developing and overseeing the implementation of binding (i.e., compulsory) operational directives to Federal Agencies to implement OMB-issued policies, principles, standards, and guidelines on information security in general.
